chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about al-sukna (habitation/endowment for residence) and al-'umra (lifetime usufruct), so he said: 'If he designated the habitation for his own lifetime, then it is as he stipulated. And if he designated it for himself and his offspring after him until his offspring perish, then it is not for them to sell it, nor to bequeath it. Then the house returns to its first owner.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَى: Lifetime usufruct or grant for life

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between sukna and umra in Shia inheritance and property law?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between temporary habitation grants and perpetual endowments, emphasizing that conditional grants to descendants restrict their right to alienate or bequeath the property. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the donor's intent, ensuring that if the lineage ends, the asset reverts to the original owner rather than becoming permanent private property. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic endowment (waqf) structures in balancing charitable intent with familial provision.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzeyl, from Abu Al Sabbah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>

was asked about the habitation and the lifetime (gifting), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he makes the habitation during his lifetime, so it is as he has stipulated it, and if makes it for him and for his offspring from after him until his offspring die, so it is not for them that they sell it, nor for it to be inherited.  Then the house would revert back to its first owner’.
en.sarwar: 22. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma’il from Muhammad ibn ai-Fudayi from abu af-Sabbah ai-Kinaniy who has narrated the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

was asked about al-Sukna ’ and al-‘Umra’ (permission to use a house for a certain period of time). He (the Imam) said, ‘If permission to use the house is given for his lifetime, then it must remain as the condition requires, if it is for his and the lifetime of those whom he leaves behind until they die, then they cannot sell it or inherit it, but they must return the house to its first owner.’”
